sections.html:
Look for the red-roofed Administration Building in downtown White Cloud, across the street from the post office. The register works from 1087 Newell Street (mail to box 885, ZIP 49349), answers at 231-689-7246 and keeps a fax line at 231-689-7271. Doors are open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. Call ahead if you are driving a long way, since staff can confirm what to bring.

Deed records are indexed back to 1910, and the books themselves reach 1840, so an old family parcel often has a paper trail worth pulling before a sale. The office takes deeds, mortgages, land contracts, trusts and other papers about real property. It supplies no abstracts, forms or notary service, and it cannot tell you when a house was built because it handles land records only.

Photocopies and faxes are turned away. Only an original with live signatures is recorded, and a self-addressed stamped envelope gets the recorded paper back to you. Fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed to you later.

Newaygo County counter payment methods
Payment methodSurcharge
Cash or checkNone
Debit or credit card, $100 or less$3.50
Debit or credit card, over $1003.5%

E-recording follows the Michigan eRecording Standards that took effect January 1, 2014. The county handles e-filed documents from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and takes ACH payment, though the filing vendor may bill extra. Providers are CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.

  • Left out of e-recording: court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys.
  • On paper, a court document or death certificate must be certified, since a plain true copy is refused.
  • A sheriff's deed goes on record within 20 days of the sale, so call the sheriff's office for sale details before bringing it in.

The rates are $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied after a price is rounded up to the next $500. The grantor pays.

A deed has to state total consideration, with any exemption written beside it, or both taxes are collected. Exchanges are taxed on the actual value of each parcel, and land lying in two counties gets a price split with tax paid to each. Stamps are bought only where the parcel is located, and filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit costs nothing.

Grantor and grantee name searches cost nothing, and you can use the books yourself even though staff will not run searches for you. A tract index search starts from a legal description, which the county equalization department or your township can supply. A parcel number works too.

Everything recorded is public, so a buyer's title agent will see your deed, any mortgage discharge and any recorded survey. The register has a survey of your lot only if someone recorded one, and it knows lot dimensions only for recorded subdivisions and site condominiums. A deed describes the land, not the buildings on it. A new street address comes from the equalization department, not this office.

A fraud alert signup page on the county site suits owners of land they seldom visit.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Newaygo County
sections.html:
West Michigan's Newaygo County covers 862 square miles, 813 of them land, with more than 230 natural lakes and 350 miles of rivers and streams. Over half the county lies within the Manistee National Forest. Fremont, Newaygo and White Cloud are the main towns, and White Cloud is the county seat.

The July 2025 population estimate is 51,622, up 3.3% from 2020. Owners occupy 86.5% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $186,700 in 2020 to 2024, and the median renter paid $904.

  • The register keeps plat books, which matter for lake lots in platted subdivisions.
  • Confirm the township before advertising a lake property, because the township assessor holds the tax record.

Summer cottage residents are common here, and anglers come for steelhead in spring and salmon in fall. Camping, hunting, cross-country skiing, cycling, birding and ORV riding fill the Manistee National Forest, so a listing that sits near public land should say so.

A seller with an old parcel near Fremont or Newaygo may find early plats and deeds in the register's books, which reach back to 1840. Check the dates on your own paperwork before you list, and note any recorded plat for a lake lot so buyers can see the lot lines.

Expect the buyer's taxable value to rise. Michigan resets it at the next assessment to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer has 45 days to notify the assessor. Close relatives who keep a residence non-commercial are excepted.

The township assessor, not the register, holds the tax record for a lake or forest-edge property, so confirm which township the parcel is in before you list. A new street address comes from the equalization department. Once the deed is recorded, the register's index shows your sale, and the buyer's name appears on the next tax roll.

Ask the Newaygo County treasurer for a tax statement, and for the certification that has to be stamped before a warranty deed can be recorded.

sections.h2: Getting a deed ready for White Cloud
sections.html:
Order the tax certification first, then have the deed prepared with the exact legal description and every owner's name. Sign before a notary, since the register provides no notary service. Bring the original, the transfer tax and a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded paper mailed back. Pay by cash or check to avoid the card surcharge. Because fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed, have the payment ready before you arrive or before the title agent sends the package.

If the sale is for cash and the buyer's agent handles the filing, ask when the deed will be filed and confirm it was indexed under the right names afterward.

If you inherited the parcel or it has been in the family for decades, pull the earlier deeds first. The books reach back to 1840 and the deed index to 1910, and the register will not run searches for you, so use the free name search yourself or have your title company do it. Finding a missing owner or an old easement before the buyer's title agent does saves time and avoids a delayed closing.

When land lies in two counties, plan on splitting the price and paying transfer tax to each. If an exemption applies, such as a corrective deed, write it on the deed so the tax is not collected by default.

faqs.q: When does the Newaygo County register of deeds close for the day?
faqs.a: The counter is open until 5 p.m. on weekdays. E-recorded documents are processed between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., so a late file waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: How is Newaygo County transfer tax calculated?
faqs.a: The county charges $1.10 per $1,000 and the state $7.50 per $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500. The seller pays it.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for paying by card at the counter?
faqs.a: Yes: $3.50 on payments up to $100, and 3.5% of the payment above that. Cash and check carry no surcharge, and recording fees cannot be billed.

faqs.q: Can a sheriff's deed or death certificate be e-recorded here?
faqs.a: No. The e-recording rules exclude court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys, so those arrive on paper, certified where required.

faqs.q: Will the register record a photocopy of my signed deed?
faqs.a: No. Only originals with live signatures are accepted, and a court document needs the court's certification.
